title: Geotopo route map

nodes.label: manifold foundations
nodes.summary: Boundary and smooth-manifold building blocks supply the ambient spaces.

nodes.label: local collars
nodes.summary: Local collar charts and their smooth diffeomorphisms are available.
nodes.remaining: Global collar existence is a separate theorem.

nodes.label: global gluing
nodes.summary: Glue along boundaries, then construct connected sums and knot complements.
nodes.remaining: Assemble global collars and the gluing interface.

nodes.label: PL groupoid
nodes.summary: The chart-based piecewise-linear structure track.
nodes.remaining: Relate chart-based PL structures to combinatorial triangulations.

nodes.label: locally flat embeddings
nodes.summary: Local flatness and local bicollars provide tame topological embeddings.

nodes.label: global bicollars
nodes.summary: Global collars of embedded spheres are needed for Annulus-type statements.
nodes.remaining: The global existence statement goes beyond a local slice chart.

nodes.label: metric / curvature
nodes.summary: Riemannian structures consume manifold foundations and the external Hopf–Rinow connection.
nodes.remaining: Volume and curvature interfaces remain a broad prerequisite track.

nodes.label: hyperbolic structures
nodes.summary: Hyperbolic structures, volume and isometry invariance feed three-manifold geometry.

nodes.label: Diff(M) group
nodes.summary: Composition, inverse and actions provide the algebraic group of diffeomorphisms.

nodes.label: chart-level Whitney
nodes.summary: The weak Whitney topology for maps in a single global chart.
nodes.remaining: General manifold charts and compact-source hypotheses still need assembly.

nodes.label: general Whitney topology
nodes.summary: The initial topology from all chartwise derivatives, restricted to Diff(M).
nodes.remaining: The chart-level construction is one input, not yet the general topological group.

nodes.label: smooth families → Diff
nodes.summary: A smooth family of diffeomorphisms induces a continuous map into Diff(M).
nodes.remaining: Prove the forward continuous-map interface; no unconditional converse.

nodes.label: continuous O(n+1) action
nodes.summary: Promote the sphere action to a continuous group homomorphism into Diff(Sⁿ).
nodes.remaining: Continuity needs the general topology and the isometry action.

nodes.label: Smale statement
nodes.summary: State the homotopy-equivalence target for the reference inclusion O(4) → Diff(S³).
nodes.remaining: State the sharp inclusion theorem; a separate summit requires its proof.

nodes.label: smooth circles
nodes.summary: Smooth circle embeddings are a geometric presentation over a general manifold.

nodes.label: forget orientation
nodes.summary: Our contribution quotients by a fixed orientation reversal.
nodes.remaining: This is not a quotient by arbitrary reparametrizations.

nodes.label: smooth links
nodes.summary: The proposed finite-component presentation uses pairwise-disjoint smooth circles.
nodes.remaining: Framings and link-complement interfaces remain separate work.

nodes.label: oriented Gauss codes
nodes.summary: Based oriented Gauss codes are a finite combinatorial presentation.
nodes.remaining: A valid abstract code need not be planar.

nodes.label: oriented PD codes
nodes.summary: An oriented PD-code presentation with crossing-slot and local compatibility data.
nodes.remaining: Global planar realizability is a later obligation.

nodes.label: isotopy image transport
nodes.summary: Our ambient-isotopy image-invariance attempt was closed without merging.
nodes.remaining: It cannot be counted as a landed equivalence theorem.

nodes.label: Gauss → PD
nodes.summary: A one-way conversion connects the two code presentations.
nodes.remaining: The current contribution does not by itself establish full presentation equivalence.

nodes.label: braid / grid branches
nodes.summary: Braid/Markov and Heegaard-Floer grid work are adjacent combinatorial branches.
nodes.remaining: Their interface to the diagram hub is a distinct route; no external PR cohort is included.

nodes.label: geometric ↔ diagram
nodes.summary: The expensive edge: generic projection and one-parameter general position.
nodes.remaining: Control how ambient isotopies cross diagram degeneracies.

nodes.label: presentation equivalence
nodes.summary: A spanning tree of correspondences anchored at diagrams lets invariants move between presentations.
nodes.remaining: The geometric edge and move-by-move combinatorial equivalences must meet here.

nodes.label: invariant agreement
nodes.summary: Alexander/Jones algorithms should agree across presentations and compute on small knots.
nodes.remaining: Agreement tests consume the correspondence maps.

nodes.label: framed slopes
nodes.summary: Slope parametrization exists; complete surgery also requires geometric complement data.
nodes.remaining: Intersection conventions and filling remain separate obligations.

nodes.label: link complements
nodes.summary: Compact complements need tubular neighborhoods, boundary structure and gluing.
nodes.remaining: Smooth-link presentations supply input objects, not the complement construction.

nodes.label: Dehn filling
nodes.summary: Fill a boundary torus with explicit slope and longitude conventions.
nodes.remaining: Check surgery on the unknot against the standard manifolds.

nodes.label: concordance / slice genus
nodes.summary: Relate presentations by embedded cobordisms and define slice genus faithfully.
nodes.remaining: Requires geometric knot inputs, tame discs and composition.

nodes.label: 4-manifold cobordism
nodes.summary: Gluing and the relevant four-manifold input support the slice statements.

nodes.label: eight geometries
nodes.summary: Model the Thurston geometries as geometric structures.

nodes.label: JSJ decomposition
nodes.summary: A decomposition must carry cutting and gluing data, not only a list of piece types.
nodes.remaining: Consumes geometry, torus surgery and manifold foundations.

nodes.label: handlebodies
nodes.summary: Manifolds with boundary and gluing provide handlebodies.

nodes.label: Heegaard genus
nodes.summary: Specify a splitting and take the least genus over a nonempty family.

nodes.label: foliations
nodes.summary: Plane fields need integrability and leaf data.

nodes.label: Euler class pairing
nodes.summary: A degree-two cohomology class must pair with surface classes.
nodes.remaining: Tangent bundles alone do not provide the required pairing.

nodes.label: geometric realization
nodes.summary: Realization and subdivision connect complexes to their underlying spaces.

nodes.label: simplicial collapse
nodes.summary: Elementary collapse and collapsibility supply the combinatorial vocabulary.

nodes.label: contractible 2-complex
nodes.summary: Our predicate records finite faces, dimension at most two and actual contractibility; the interval is a witness.
nodes.remaining: This contribution proves no cylinder-collapse conclusion.

nodes.label: PL ↔ combinatorial
nodes.summary: Prove that combinatorial triangulations and chart-based PL manifold structures agree.
nodes.remaining: Both directions are substantial theorems, with the correct vertex-link and subdivision conditions.

nodes.label: simplicial K × I
nodes.summary: A compatible simplicial cylinder must connect the hypothesis to the collapse vocabulary.
nodes.remaining: Construct and expose the product needed by the target statement.

nodes.label: Zeeman statement
nodes.summary: Faithfully state: a finite contractible two-complex K has collapsible K × I.
nodes.remaining: Open conjecture: a faithful statement and concrete collapse examples are milestones; no proof completion is promised.

nodes.label: Diff topological group
nodes.summary: Prove continuity of composition and inverse for the compact-manifold Whitney topology.
nodes.remaining: Requires the assembled topology; the algebraic Group instance is insufficient.

nodes.label: Diff(M, ∂M)
nodes.summary: Construct the boundary-fixing subgroup with its induced topology.
nodes.remaining: Relative isotopies and boundary conditions are needed by disk and sphere arguments.

nodes.label: parametric sphere topology
nodes.summary: The global, parameter-dependent geometric arguments in Hatcher’s proof.
nodes.remaining: A major proof development beyond topology definitions and the continuous sphere action.

nodes.label: Smale–Hatcher theorem
nodes.summary: Prove that the reference inclusion O(4) → Diff(S³) is a homotopy equivalence.
nodes.remaining: Summit proof horizon: building or stating the inclusion does not discharge it.

nodes.label: unknot filling identities
nodes.summary: Prove the 0-surgery and rational-surgery identities against the pinned slope convention.
nodes.remaining: Must recover S¹ × S² and the appropriate lens spaces with actual diffeomorphisms.

nodes.label: Property P statement
nodes.summary: Faithfully express Property P for nontrivial knots and their nontrivial surgeries.
nodes.remaining: Requires genuine complements, filling, knot equivalence and fundamental groups.

nodes.label: gauge-theory input
nodes.summary: The gauge-theoretic machinery of Kronheimer–Mrowka is a separate proof dependency.
nodes.remaining: External proof development; it is not supplied by Dehn-surgery definitions.

nodes.label: Property P theorem
nodes.summary: Formalize the theorem that a nontrivial knot has Property P.
nodes.remaining: Proof horizon after the surgery library and the deep gauge-theory input.

nodes.label: Property R statement
nodes.summary: State the characterization of the unknot by 0-surgery yielding S¹ × S².
nodes.remaining: An adjacent summit with its own proof requirements.

nodes.label: Alexander-one slicing
nodes.summary: State: Alexander polynomial one implies topological sliceness.
nodes.remaining: Normalize the polynomial and use locally flat topological disks, keeping smooth sliceness separate.

nodes.label: 4D disk embedding input
nodes.summary: Develop the four-manifold machinery supporting Freedman’s topological slicing result.
nodes.remaining: A major proof dependency beyond the predicate for a slice disk.

nodes.label: Freedman slicing theorem
nodes.summary: Prove that Alexander-polynomial-one knots bound locally flat disks in B⁴.
nodes.remaining: The proof must connect the computable polynomial, geometric presentation and four-dimensional input.

nodes.label: smooth slice obstructions
nodes.summary: Concordance invariants distinguish the smooth category from the topological category.
nodes.remaining: The Conway/Piccirillo direction also consumes external homological or other smooth obstructions.

nodes.label: prime decomposition
nodes.summary: Prime connected-sum decomposition precedes the torus decomposition.
nodes.remaining: Construct the decomposition and establish its existence and uniqueness.

nodes.label: Geometrization statement
nodes.summary: State geometric structures on the pieces, with the required prime and torus decompositions.
nodes.remaining: A list of eight labels does not supply metrics, cutting data or reconstruction.

nodes.label: Weeks minimum volume
nodes.summary: State minimum volume using an explicitly constructed Weeks manifold and metric-independent hyperbolic volume.
nodes.remaining: Requires a concrete manifold, volume integration and Mostow invariance.

nodes.label: virtual fibering
nodes.summary: State virtual fibering for closed hyperbolic three-manifolds through an actual finite cover.
nodes.remaining: Finite covering spaces, mapping tori and the hyperbolic input must meet.

nodes.label: Ricci-flow proof input
nodes.summary: The analytic and geometric machinery in Perelman’s proof is an external proof development.
nodes.remaining: The statement roadmap does not build Ricci flow, surgery analysis or the required estimates.

nodes.label: Geometrization theorem
nodes.summary: Prove the geometric decomposition theorem with genuine structures on its pieces.
nodes.remaining: Far proof horizon joining the manifold, surgery, geometry and analytic tracks.

nodes.label: surface mapping classes
nodes.summary: Control surface gluing maps up to isotopy for Heegaard splittings.
nodes.remaining: The general diffeomorphism and family APIs are shared inputs.

nodes.label: rank–genus counterexample
nodes.summary: State the existence of a three-manifold with rank π₁ strictly smaller than Heegaard genus.
nodes.remaining: Requires least genus over a proved nonempty family and the minimal-generators invariant.

nodes.label: certified genus bounds
nodes.summary: Prove the lower genus bounds and upper fundamental-group rank bounds for a concrete family.
nodes.remaining: Providing a splitting gives an upper genus bound, not the lower bound needed for a counterexample.

nodes.label: Li rank–genus theorem
nodes.summary: Formalize a concrete witness disproving rank equals Heegaard genus.
nodes.remaining: The strict inequality needs both certified estimates on the same manifold.

nodes.label: combinatorial links
nodes.summary: Recursive sphere and ball conditions define combinatorial manifolds.
nodes.remaining: Build the subdivision relations and base cases before using the comparison.

nodes.label: smooth triangulations
nodes.summary: Construct compatible triangulations of smooth manifolds.
nodes.remaining: The Whitehead/Cairns triangulation development goes far beyond an abstract realization.

nodes.label: Whitehead comparison
nodes.summary: Prove smooth-to-PL existence and the appropriate essential uniqueness, reconciled with combinatorial triangulations.
nodes.remaining: Summit proof horizon: general triangulability, PL structure and smoothability remain distinct.

nodes.label: general triangulability
nodes.summary: Triangulability means homeomorphism to the realization of some simplicial complex.
nodes.remaining: This is weaker than having a combinatorial or PL triangulation.

nodes.label: Manolescu statement
nodes.summary: State the existence of a closed topological five-manifold admitting no triangulation.
nodes.remaining: Use general triangulability; failure to admit a PL structure is a weaker conclusion.

routes.title: Knot calculus → Property P
routes.insight: Our circle and code work is the entrance. The route must cross geometric equivalence, genuine surgery and convention checks before the statement; the summit additionally needs major gauge theory.
routes.finish: Prove Property P for all nontrivial knots; a surgery definition or statement is an intermediate checkpoint.

routes.title: Diff(M) → Smale–Hatcher
routes.insight: Our single-chart topology is an early foothold. Compact-manifold topology, relative groups and parameterized geometry must be assembled before the global homotopy-equivalence proof.
routes.finish: Prove that the actual inclusion O(4) → Diff(S³) is a homotopy equivalence.

routes.title: Smooth / PL / Top comparison
routes.insight: Our contractible-complex predicate occupies the collapse branch of a much larger simplicial library. The main summit is a proved comparison of smooth and PL structures; Manolescu and Zeeman expose distinct limits of triangulation and collapse.
routes.finish: Prove the comparison and smooth-triangulation existence/uniqueness results. Zeeman remains an open-conjecture branch.

routes.title: Knot invariants → Freedman slicing
routes.insight: Our finite presentations must support invariant transport and normalized computations. Locally flat disks, concordance and the four-dimensional disk-embedding machinery are further independent obligations.
routes.finish: Prove Alexander polynomial one implies topological sliceness, while preserving the distinction from smooth sliceness.

routes.title: Surgery → Geometrization
routes.insight: Our smooth-link input can eventually reach actual three-manifolds through surgery. Geometric metrics, prime/JSJ decompositions and a large analytic proof program are separate mountains; Weeks volume and virtual fibering branch off the same infrastructure.
routes.finish: Prove geometric decomposition with real cutting/gluing data and geometric structures; the Ricci-flow proof dependency is external.

routes.title: Gluing → rank versus genus
routes.insight: Our Whitney work can feed the isotopy and surface-gluing interfaces. A counterexample needs a genuine minimal Heegaard genus and certified lower bounds; drawing one splitting supplies only an upper bound.
routes.finish: Prove rank π₁(M) < Heegaard genus(M) for a concrete witness, formalizing Li’s counterexample.

horizonNote: The cited roadmap targets faithful statements. These six proof summits are editorial long-term extensions: intermediate statement gates remain visible, and no external proof machinery is claimed implemented. Zeeman is an open conjecture, not a proof task.
